title: Three ways of not answering
lede: I wasn't told, I cannot be made to say, and the question never got asked properly: three moves for the three ways of not answering.
body: Three moves, one idea. [Unawares](/moves/unawares/) is I was not told. [Plead the Fifth](/moves/plead-the-fifth/) is I cannot be made to say. [Depositioning](/moves/depositioning/) is the question never got asked properly. They file in chapter III because they are the same character in three costumes, and because that chapter was the thinnest in the book and the one most in need of the vocabulary of the non-answer.

The Fifth is the entry to read carefully. The privilege is real, it is old, and the guide is not against it. The move is what the right becomes when it is the only sentence in the answer, offered in a hearing where what is at stake is a headline, not a cell.

Each carries a source: plausible deniability, the amendment itself, and Rule 30 on depositions. Each is also wired to the thing it answers. The subpoena now points at both moves that meet it, and the secret meeting at the move that hides inside it, because a reader who finds one half of a mechanism should be able to reach the other from the page.
Chapter III has the vocabulary it was missing. It is still the shortest chapter, and it is no longer the least useful.
